//: Benchmark manifest — DATA, not code. Add/remove/rename models here; the
runner never hard-codes a tag.
JSON, not YAML, DELIBERATELY. PyYAML is absent on this host and the repo's
yaml-dependent tests run inside the LiteLLM container to get it. This
harness cannot: it must control Ollama model residency and read host memory
and swap, which are not visible from inside a container. Zero dependencies
beats a hand-rolled parser for a nested document.
RESEARCHED, not assumed. Logical names map to Ollama's top-level `think`.
KNOWN UPSTREAM CONSTRAINTS (github issues, verified against local measurement):
* ollama/ollama#13353 — Qwen renderers IGNORE the think parameter. Our probe
measured qwen3.5 standard==deep (765/765 chars); the cause is the renderer,
not the model. Qwen is effectively 2-mode (off / on) on Ollama today.
* Thinking level 'medium' is reported unsupported for Qwen on Ollama; only
off/on are honoured. A 3-level sweep on Qwen measures the same thing twice.
* ABSENCE of `think` means thinking ENABLED (Ollama default), so a 'default'
mode is a thinking run, not a neutral one. Do not treat it as baseline.
* BerriAI/litellm#15059 — reasoning_effort is accepted and dropped unmapped;
this is why config/litellm/reasoning_router.py translates it to `think`.
* gpt-oss: think=false does not silence it (measured 111 chars). Its real
lever is the SYSTEM PROMPT ('Reasoning: low|medium|high'), which gives 3
monotonic levels. See model_settings.
CONSEQUENCE: 'deep' is only meaningful for models with a working level control
(gpt-oss via system prompt; gemma4 measured distinct). For Qwen, run off/standard
only -- the probe already skips ignored modes with a machine-readable reason.
Only seed is now fixed across models. Sampling comes from model_settings,
because comparing models at one vendor's temperature measures the
temperature. Seed keeps a single model's runs reproducible.
VENDOR-CORRECT settings, APPLIED by default. Each model competes at the
settings its vendor documents, because the question is which model deserves
a role -- not which survives someone else's temperature. Sources are on each
entry. `system_prefix` is the model's native reasoning lever where sampling
params are not it (gpt-oss).
num_predict follows vendor guidance where given: Qwen recommends 32768 for
most queries, so reasoning-heavy suites get it rather than an 8192 ceiling
that would truncate thinking and score it as a wrong answer.

context_targets_note: Context ceilings are read from Ollama /api/show (gemma4/qwen 262144, gpt-oss 131072) and were NOT cross-checked against vendor documentation. Ollama's advertised context can differ from a model's trained context; the probe measures what is ACTUALLY accepted, which is the number used.

//: IDEAL vs PRACTICAL context are different numbers and the difference matters
on a 64 GB machine.
IDEAL = the model's native trained window (context_native above).
PRACTICAL = what fits alongside weights without paging. KV cache is allocated
per slot as num_ctx x OLLAMA_NUM_PARALLEL, so a 262,144 window on a 26B model
does not fit in 64 GB and would swap -- which this project already measured as
the cause of a 13-minute stall.
MEASURED resident cost on this machine (weights + KV at the stated ctx):
gemma4:26b-mlx  17.5G @16K   22.1G @98K
gpt-oss:20b     11.9G @16K
So the benchmark sweeps 24K-64K: inside every model's native window, and
inside what 64 GB holds without paging. Native ceilings are recorded so a
128 GB profile can raise them on evidence rather than on the spec sheet.
context_policy.rationale: within native window for all models AND resident on 64 GB
